text:
akshay: Quick signal from today's load test: paged-attn with small block_size=64 under high sequence variance is causing lots of micro-evicts and a perf cliff (latency tail and occasional OOM).

maria: Ugh, saw that on a customer trace too. Can you paste the flame/profile?

akshay: Dropped a short perfdump in the thread. Key points: compaction time is dominating when we try to coalesce many tiny free ranges, and the allocator spends cycles scanning buckets. CPU-side kernel selection flips to the fallback kernel mid-request because workspace estimate grows.

ell en: Can you share the KV cache hit distribution? Might be related to eviction churn.
akshay: KV hit rate is fine overall (~82%) but there are hot streams that continuously touch new blocks, causing fragmentation. The paged block reuse allocator tries to salvage partial blocks but our compaction threshold triggers full copy compaction too often.

paul: Ideas: 1) implement a "salvage-first" opportunistic reclaim that extracts contiguous subranges without full compaction; 2) add a lightweight bitmap to each block to speed free-range detection; 3) introduce a watermark to prevent kernel fallback by reserving a tiny extra workspace for worst-case transient growth.
maria: I prototyped (2) a while back — bitmap reduced compaction scan by ~40% in microbench. We didn't hook it to the eviction policy though.
akshay: Sketching a combined approach: salvage-first + soft-evict watermark + adaptive block_sizing on hot streams. Pseudocode for the eviction heuristic I tested:

```
if fragment_pct > 30% and active_streams < 4:
  salvage_contiguous_ranges()
elif fragment_pct > 60%:
  schedule_full_compaction(async=true)
else:
  prefer_block_reuse()
```

runtime-bot: Perf alert: paged-attn kernel fallback triggered 14 times in last 10m for pool:gpu-a1

ellen: Salvage-first needs to be O(1) in the common case. If it's doing memcopies for each tiny subrange we lose the win. Maybe coalesce at remap time (defer physical copies until threshold).

paul: Also saw that batching heuristics exacerbate it — large batches cause longer-lived KV entries so eviction churn overlaps with slow compaction. We should bias batch packing to prefer requests with higher KV hit probability when fragmentation is high.
maria: Agree. We can add a batch_score = hit_prob - frag_penalty and let the scheduler prefer higher score in that pool.
akshay: Logged some numbers from the test run:
- baseline (block_size=64): p95 latency 420ms, p99 1.9s, throughput 320 tok/s
- salvage-first + bitmap: p95 260ms, p99 640ms, throughput 480 tok/s
- salvage-first + watermark(8MB extra): p95 210ms, p99 310ms, throughput 510 tok/s

infra-ci: Run note: test job 1987654300 archived at https://ci.internal/runs/1987654300 (contains perfdump + heapmap).

maria: Nice. Any regression risks? What about memory overhead of bitmap + watermark?
akshay: Bitmap adds ~1-2% memory per block; watermark is configurable per pool and has strict bounded reservation. I also found a corner-case where async compaction + kernel fallback interact — compaction wins a race and frees workspace mid-generation causing a tiny corruption in a stress test. Repro steps in the perfdump.

ell en: We should add a lightweight correctness guard: when async compaction frees memory, signal kernel-selection to re-evaluate and delay applying reclaimed region until the current request's kernel has safely finished. Cheap fence.

paul: Action items:
- akshay: land salvage-first POC + bitmap (bench + unit tests)
- maria: add batch scoring hook into scheduler and run A/B against high-frag traces
- ellen: implement compaction->kernel fence and add a stress test to perf harness
- infra-ci: schedule a canary on dedicated pool next week (low risk)

akshay: I'll open PRs and link test artifacts here. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

runtime-bot: Note: rolling canary scheduled for pool:gpu-a1 on 1988-05-02 03:00 UTC

paul: follow-up: we might also expose "block_salvage_policy" as an opt-in feature flag for Dedicated customers who prioritize latency.
maria: +1. Might help some enterprise workloads.
akshay: PRs linked: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4021 and https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4022

ell en: left review comments, nothing blocking.

paul: Great thread. We'll track regressions in the next perf run and reconvene if any kernel fallback alerts persist.
